blocks.text: ILIGAN CITY – Halloween, traditionally observed through scary stories and images. need not be spooky. This is the message put across by the Catholic diocese here on Saturday, as the nation prepares to observe All Saints’ Day and All Souls’ Day on Sunday and Monday, respectively. As a counter-event, the diocese held its own version of the Halloween observance. But instead of scary and spooky costumes, participants dressed as saints during the “Dress Like a Saint” parade organized by St. Michael’s Cathedral on Saturday afternoon.
